providers.name: Google Maps Platform
notes: Google Maps Platform is a family of separate APIs. Each endpoint here names its actual service: Places API (New), Routes API, Geocoding API, or Directions API (Legacy). Each must be enabled separately in a Cloud project with billing.

Places API (New) and Routes API require a response field mask (X-Goog-FieldMask header). Omitting it returns an error. The fields requested also determine the billing tier (Essentials, Pro, Enterprise, Enterprise + Atmosphere).
Search responses wrap results in a places array, so search field masks use a places. prefix; Place Details returns a single Place, so its mask has no prefix.

Places API (legacy), Directions API and Distance Matrix API were given Legacy status on March 1, 2025 (replacements: Places API (New) and Routes API). Google's legacy overview says legacy services are not available in new Cloud projects; the Directions page itself states that as of October 2026 Directions API (Legacy) can no longer be enabled for new projects. Cut-off details are per product, so check each product page. The library includes Directions (Legacy) only as a clearly flagged distractor.
Photo resource names from Places responses cannot be cached and may expire. Author attributions must be displayed with photos.
Routes API durations are strings of seconds with an 's' suffix ("1150s"); distanceMeters is always meters regardless of units.
Geocoding is modeled with the v3 web-service format; the documentation notes that Geocoding API v4 is generally available.

endpoints.title: Compute Route Matrix
endpoints.description: Returns travel distance and duration for every combination of a list of origins and a list of destinations, for one travel mode per request. The response is a JSON array with one element per origin/destination pair; elements are not guaranteed to be in order, so each element includes originIndex and destinationIndex. Elements contain no route polyline or turn-by-turn steps. Limits: origins x destinations at most 625 elements (at most 100 for TRANSIT or TRAFFIC_AWARE_OPTIMAL), and at most 50 waypoints given as place IDs or addresses.

parameters.name: X-Goog-FieldMask
parameters.description: Comma-separated element fields to return, without a prefix (for example originIndex,destinationIndex,status,condition,distanceMeters,duration). Required. Include status, otherwise every element appears OK. The wildcard * is discouraged in production.

parameters.name: origins
parameters.description: Matrix rows. Each item is a RouteMatrixOrigin: {"waypoint": Waypoint, "routeModifiers": optional}. A Waypoint sets exactly one of location ({"latLng": {...}}), placeId or address.

parameters.name: destinations
parameters.description: Matrix columns. Each item is a RouteMatrixDestination: {"waypoint": Waypoint}.

parameters.name: travelMode
parameters.description: Mode of transportation for every element (unspecified defaults to DRIVE). WALK, BICYCLE and TWO_WHEELER routes are in beta, and apps must display a warning for them. (TRUCK, which needs vehicle information, is not modeled here.)

parameters.name: routingPreference
parameters.description: Traffic handling. Only valid when travelMode is DRIVE or TWO_WHEELER; otherwise the request fails.

parameters.name: departureTime
parameters.description: RFC 3339 timestamp; defaults to the request time. Past times are allowed only for TRANSIT. Cannot be combined with arrivalTime.

parameters.name: arrivalTime
parameters.description: RFC 3339 timestamp for when the traveler wants to arrive. Only for TRANSIT. Cannot be combined with departureTime.

parameters.name: transitPreferences
parameters.description: Only for TRANSIT: {"allowedTravelModes": [BUS | SUBWAY | TRAIN | LIGHT_RAIL | RAIL], "routingPreference": LESS_WALKING | FEWER_TRANSFERS}. RAIL is shorthand for subway, train and light rail.

parameters.name: units
parameters.description: Units for display fields (localizedValues). distanceMeters is always meters.

parameters.name: languageCode
parameters.description: BCP-47 language for display values. If omitted, inferred from the first origin.

parameters.name: regionCode
parameters.description: Two-character ccTLD region code.

parameters.name: extraComputations
parameters.description: Extra values to compute; the matching response fields must also be in the field mask.

arrivalTime is only allowed with TRANSIT.

expansionNotes: Autocomplete (New) (places:autocomplete) is part of Places API (New). Unlike Nearby Search, Text Search and Place Details, its documentation lists the response field mask under OPTIONAL parameters; the other Places (New) and Routes methods modeled here require one.

Autocomplete (New) sessions: the app generates a session token (Google recommends a version 4 UUID; the reference requires a URL- and filename-safe base64 string of at most 36 ASCII characters) and passes the same token to each Autocomplete (New) request and to the Place Details (New) request (sessionToken query parameter) that ends the session. Sessions group the typing and selection phases for billing.

Routes API computeRouteMatrix (POST https://routes.googleapis.com/distanceMatrix/v2:computeRouteMatrix) returns one element per origin/destination pair. Over REST the response body is a JSON array; elements are not guaranteed to be in order, so each element carries originIndex and destinationIndex. Include status in the field mask, otherwise every element appears OK.
computeRouteMatrix limits: origins x destinations <= 625 elements (<= 100 for TRANSIT or TRAFFIC_AWARE_OPTIMAL), and at most 50 waypoints given as place IDs or addresses.

Routes API transit options: arrivalTime applies only to TRANSIT and cannot be combined with departureTime; transitPreferences (allowedTravelModes, routingPreference LESS_WALKING / FEWER_TRANSFERS) applies only to TRANSIT; routingPreference applies only to DRIVE and TWO_WHEELER. Transit trips are available for up to 7 days in the past or 100 days in the future.

Place resources also document accessibilityOptions (wheelchairAccessibleEntrance/Parking/Restroom/Seating), goodForChildren, allowsDogs, outdoorSeating, restroom and parkingOptions. The original Places endpoints in this library do not list these fields in responseFields, so the expansion scenarios do not use them.

explanation.summary: Nearby Search (New) is a POST request whose JSON body describes a circle (center + radius in meters) in locationRestriction, the place types to include, the maximum result count and the ranking. The X-Goog-FieldMask header chooses which Place fields come back. The response is an object with a places array.
keyIdeas: Some APIs take parameters in a JSON request body rather than the URL.
A required header (the field mask) controls both the response contents and the price.
Search field masks use the places. prefix because results are wrapped in the places array.
Bias (soft) and restriction (hard) are different; the requirement 'strictly within' demands a restriction.
